B01.capture_spec: C01: lab-shaders/17-crosshair.gdshader, a ColorRect on a square canvas, Forward+, 30 fps, `--length` = the measured audio of B01 (about 13 s). Keyframes as fractions of the clip, the dials in file order: hold the defaults to 4 %; dot_size, ring_distance, ring_width one after another from 4 % to 44 % (13.3 % each: 4.4 % up to 1.0, 4.4 % hold, 4.4 % back to its default); hold the defaults from 44 % to 56 % (the 50 % frame is inside this hold; the voice says 'No picture file sits behind it'); arm_gap 56 to 67 % (up to 59.5, hold to 63.5, back to 67), arm_length 67 to 78 % (up to 70.5, hold to 74.5, back to 78), arm_width 78 to 96 % (up to 83, hold at 1.0 to 91 so the 85 % frame is a hold, back to 96); hold 96 % to 100 %. Scripted.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Inside or Outside' (serif 40) top-left of the stage. A real Godot render of the finished crosshair in a SQUARE framed window on the cream stage; a script moves the six dials one after another, each out to 1.0 and back to its default (dot size, ring distance, ring width, then a pause at the defaults, then arm gap, arm length, arm width). At the top-left of the window a readout 'no picture file' lands as the pause begins; under the window a one-line caption defines the node the shader paints: 'Color Rect: a flat rectangle the shader paints'.
B01.motion_claim: Each dial moves in turn and the crosshair reshapes with it, so the shape is plainly made by rules and not by a picture; the pause lands on the words 'no picture file'.

show.event: crosshair at its defaults, window labelled; the caption defines Color Rect
the first three dials move, one after another
the dials pause at their defaults; readout 'no picture file' lands
the last three dials move
back at the defaults

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a crosshair with six dial icons
B01.why: A real render is the honest proof of 'drawn by a shader, no picture file'; a drawing would only claim it.
B01.sparse_reason: Result-only layout: a square Godot window centred on the 16:9 stage; the underfill is by design because the window is the subject. Only the underfill check is waived.

B02.visual_intent: A 13-by-13 grid of outline cells centred on the stage (the pixel grid), the label 'fragment() · once per pixel' above it. One cell near the middle gets a terracotta ring and a small tag 'my address'; the tag then changes to 'inside?'. Then every cell answers at once: cells within five cells of the middle fill teal ('yes'), the rest stay empty ('no'), and a circle with a stepped edge appears out of the answers. Caption: 'yes: on · no: off'.
B02.motion_claim: One cell is handed its own address and asks 'inside?', then every cell answers yes or no at the same instant and a circle appears out of the answers.

show.event: grid and the label 'fragment() · once per pixel'
one cell ringed, tag 'my address'
the tag becomes 'inside?'
all cells answer at once; the teal circle forms
caption 'yes: on · no: off'

B02.why: Yes-or-no answers from every cell forming a circle is the whole idea, and a grid shows it at cell level; the real render arrives in a few beats.

B03.visual_intent: A square (the UV square) on the cream stage with an 'across · 0 to 1' axis along the top and a 'down · 0 to 1' axis down the left side, the second axis pointing DOWN. A terracotta cross at the middle labelled 'center · 0.5, 0.5'. A teal dot drops in to the lower right of the center, labelled 'this pixel · 0.62, 0.66'.
B03.motion_claim: The center marker appears, then the pixel's dot drops onto the square and its address label counts up to 0.62, 0.66.

show.event: the square with its two axes
center marker and its label
pixel dot drops in; its address label counts up to 0.62, 0.66

B03.why: An address is a position on a square; a dot with a live label is the clearest picture of it.

B04.visual_intent: The square zooms to the center and the pixel; a caption defines the word: 'distance: how far apart two points are'. A right triangle is drawn between them: the horizontal leg labelled 0.12, the vertical leg labelled 0.16, the long side between center and pixel. Beside it the arithmetic types in as MathTex, line by line: 0.12² + 0.16², then = 0.0144 + 0.0256 = 0.04, then √0.04, then = 0.2. The long side takes the label 'distance 0.2' and a terracotta ring.
B04.motion_claim: The two legs draw in, the arithmetic lands line by line, and the long side takes its label.

show.event: the square zooms to the center and the pixel; caption defines distance
the horizontal leg draws, labelled 0.12
the vertical leg draws, labelled 0.16 [quick: 0.35 s at most, done by 0.44]
the arithmetic starts: 0.12² + 0.16²
= 0.2; the long side labelled 'distance 0.2' and ringed

B04.why: A triangle with its legs and long side is the geometry of a distance; the numbers then land on it as they are spoken.

cues.label: distance: how far apart. vec2(0.5) is the center

B06.visual_intent: A plot on the cream stage: the x axis 'across the shape' from 0 to 1, the y axis 'distance from the middle' from 0 to 0.5. A V-shaped teal curve (0.5 at both ends, 0 at x = 0.5). A horizontal terracotta line at 0.3 labelled 'radius 0.3'. A grey dot starts on the V at the left end, above the line; it then rides the V to the right, turning teal under the line, and the stretch of the x axis where the V lies under the line (x from 0.2 to 0.8) lights up and is labelled 'inside'.
B06.motion_claim: The V draws in, the radius line slides down to 0.3, a dot rides the V and turns teal under the line, and the stretch of the axis beneath it lights up as 'inside'.

B06.why: A function against a threshold line is a plot; the lit stretch under the line is the claim.

B07.visual_intent: A small plot: the x axis 'value' from 0 to 0.6, the y axis 'output' from 0 to 1. A vertical terracotta line at 0.3 labelled 'edge'. A dot labelled 'value' starts left of the edge with a readout beside it. The step curve draws in two stretches: output 0 left of the edge, then output 1 from the edge on, labelled 'step(edge, x)'. The dot slides across the edge and the readout flips from 0 to 1. Caption (the glossary's wording): '0 below the edge, 1 from the edge up'.
B07.motion_claim: A dot slides along the axis and the output jumps from 0 to 1 at the edge.

B08.visual_intent: A row of 25 pixel cells with centres at x = 0.02, 0.06, ... 0.98 (cells 5 to 19, the ones within 0.3 of the middle, are inside; no cell lies exactly on 0.3) with the V profile above it and the radius line. Below, a row of 0 and 1 values. First the label 'step(0.3, d)' and the small question 'd ≥ radius?': inside cells read 0 (empty), outside cells read 1 (teal), a hole. Then the two inputs trade places in the label to 'step(d, 0.3)', the question becomes 'radius ≥ d?' and the row flips: inside cells read 1 (teal), outside cells 0 (empty). Cells are numbered from 0. A terracotta ring marks cell 17, a pixel at distance 0.2 like ours (our own pixel is off this row), throughout. At the end the teal stretch is labelled 'the circle'.
B08.motion_claim: The two inputs trade places and the row of ones and zeros flips inside out.

B08.why: The flip happens to a whole row at once, so the motion is the claim; the real circle follows in the next beat.
